opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants

amount.raw: Grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Individuals from low-income households in Scotland who are ineligible for government tuition fee funding, ordinarily resident in Scotland (or with a substantial recent connection), entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK (or asylum seekers), enrolled on an undergraduate degree course at an eligible Scottish higher education institution
opportunities.summary: Grants covering tuition fees for students from low-income households who are ineligible for Scottish Government tuition fee support, including those returning to study after withdrawing and asylum seekers. Portal open 1 June 2026 to 5pm 1 December 2026 for academic year 2026-27.

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship

amount.raw: Full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants plus an additional living-cost bursary of £1,200

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households, ordinarily resident in Scotland with a meaningful connection, entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, accepted onto the MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (jointly delivered by Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh and University of Edinburgh), who have not already obtained a postgraduate degree
opportunities.summary: Scholarship in partnership with the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh covering full tuition fees and a £1,200 living-cost bursary for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants, aimed at widening participation in postgraduate plant science/botany study for Scottish graduates from low-income households.
